  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   -A youraccount
#   -J SM_HSP_dimer_prod
#   --error=job.%j.err
#   --output=job.%j.out
#   -t 24:00:00
#   -n 20
#   -c 1

#flux: --job-name=SM_HSP_dimer_prod
#flux: -n 20
#flux: -c 1
#flux: --time-limit=24h

ml ABINIT/8.10.3 Armadillo/9.700.2 CDO/1.9.5 GOTM/5.3-221-gac7ec88d NCO/4.8.1 NCO/4.9.2 OpenFOAM/6 OpenFOAM/7 OpenFOAM/v1912 Rosetta/3.7 Siesta/4.1-MaX-1.0 Siesta/4.1-b4 Singular/4.1.2 XCrySDen/1.5.60 XCrySDen/1.6.2 deal.II/9.1.1-gcc deal.II/9.1.1-intel

gmx grompp -f md.mdp -c npt.gro -t npt.cpt -p topol.top -o md_0_1.tpr

# Under Flux, launch within the allocation.
# If your site requires launch via Flux, use flux-run for containment/accounting.
flux run -n 1 -c 20 gmx mdrun -nt 20 -deffnm md_0_1

reasons: The resource section requests 20 tasks with 1 core each (`#flux: -n 20`, `#flux: -c 1`), but the intended workload is a single Gromacs run using 20 threads (`mdrun -nt 20`). This is a resource mismatch: it should request 1 task with 20 cores (or equivalent), otherwise 19 tasks are allocated unnecessarily and placement/accounting may be incorrect.
issues: The launch line uses `flux run -n 1 -c 20 ...` which conflicts with the batch allocation (`#flux: -n 20 -c 1`). Depending on Flux configuration, this may oversubscribe, fail, or ignore the requested per-command resources.
